query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a high spin‐orbit coupling element such as Pt (≈50 at.%) into the FeCoNi-based alloy will induce L1₀ chemical ordering—specifically, by promoting chemical short-range order—which enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy and significantly increases the coercivity relative to the single-phase fcc state.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a similarly composed high-entropy alloy thin film exhibiting high saturation magnetization with coercivity below 100 Oe.
generation.intervention: Alloy the base FeCoNi system with approximately 50 at.% Pt during film deposition followed by rapid thermal annealing (RTA) to promote L1₀ ordering.
generation.conditions: Thin films sputter-deposited on thermally oxidized Si/SiO₂ substrates at room temperature, then subjected to a defined RTA treatment; composition constrained to a high-entropy alloy system based on FeCoNi with Pt addition; magnetic measurements performed at room temperature using standard VSM protocols.
generation.structural_mediator: Transformation from a high-symmetry fcc structure to a low-symmetry L1₀ (tetragonal) phase induced by Pt incorporation.
generation.mechanism: Pt addition reduces the crystal symmetry and introduces strong spin-orbit coupling, which enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy; the resulting L1₀ ordering, a manifestation of chemical short-range order governed by multicomponent mixing, increases domain wall pinning, leading to a substantial increase in coercivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significant enhancement in coercivity (potentially increasing by over an order of magnitude, well beyond 100 Oe) while maintaining or only modestly affecting the high saturation magnetization of the original fcc alloy.
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its derived high-entropy alloy counterpart with coercivity values in the range of 10–100 Oe.
generation.boundary: This intervention applies to sputtered thin film samples on oxidized Si substrates with controlled composition and post-deposition RTA processing; measurements are to be taken at room temperature using VSM; the study is limited to high-entropy alloy phases where L1₀ ordering is achievable without compromising the bulk chemical disorder necessary for high saturation magnetization.
generation.uncertainty: The precise optimal Pt content and RTA parameters for maximizing coercivity without excessive loss in magnetization remain to be determined; it is also uncertain how well this approach will translate from thin films to bulk materials.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of thin film samples under identical sputtering conditions on thermally oxidized Si/SiO₂ substrates: one set of pure fcc FeCoNi (or its standard high-entropy derivative) and a second set with 50 at.% Pt added. Subject both sets to identical rapid thermal annealing treatments. Characterize the crystallographic phase using X-ray diffraction to confirm L1₀ ordering in the Pt-containing samples, and measure magnetic hysteresis loops using vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM).
measurements: XRD analysis for phase identification (fcc vs. L1₀)
Coercivity (Hc) values from magnetic hysteresis loops
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Pt-added samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in coercivity (e.g., an increase greater than 200% compared to the control) and/or if XRD fails to confirm the formation of the L1₀ ordered phase, then the hypothesis that Pt addition overcomes the coercivity limitation through induced anisotropy is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractThe vast high entropy alloy (HEA) composition space is promising for discovery of new material phases with unique properties. This study explores the potential to achieve rare‐earth‐free high magnetic anisotropy materials in single‐phase HEA thin films. Thin films of FeCoNiMnCu sputtered on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates at room temperature are magnetically soft, with a coercivity on the order of 10 Oe. After post‐deposition rapid thermal annealing (RTA), the films exhibit a single face‐centered‐cubic phase, with an almost 40‐fold increase in coercivity. Inclusion of 50 at.% Pt in the film leads to ordering of a single L10 high entropy intermetallic phase after RTA, along with high magnetic anisotropy and 3 orders of magnitude coercivity increase. While the combination of saturation magnetization and coercivity for these RTA‐ treated FeCoNiMnCu films is impressive in comparison to previously reported bulk systems, the coercivity is still modest, due to the high symmetry of the cubic lattice which limits the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy. The facilitation of low‐symmetry chemical order and crystal structure combined with strong spin‐orbit coupling is in general necessary to realize strong magnetocrysalline anisotropy. To achieve these conditions in a high entropy system, we have added 50 at.% Pt to the FeCoNiMnCu alloy, employing the high entropy intermetallic design approach in search of highly anisotropic L10 ordering. Although the certainty of Pt sites reduces the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, we demonstrate below that such optimized entropy can still stabilize a single high‐entropy L10 phase.

In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.
